subject: Instrumentation gaps: per-route cost & latency slices + owner runbook
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com, eng@platformops.io
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Instrumentation gaps: per-route cost & latency slices + owner runbook

Hi team,

Quick background: Acme has surfaced a production incident where their per-tenant cost reports (per-route slices) look wildly off for a handful of routes. They provided the attached CSV with sample token-paths and a heatmap screenshot. From a console/observability perspective we think this is two problems: (1) missing route-level cost attribution in some routers, and (2) a gap in our slice sampling that undercounts tail latencies.

I need a concrete, small-scope runbook we can follow to:
- Triage and confirm which routes are missing attribution (steps + queries)
- Re-run sampling with increased tail capture for the impacted tenants
- Short-term mitigation to surface accurate billable metrics in the Console while we fix instrumentation

Asks: can each of you own one part of this by EOD Friday? Proposed split: Marcus — confirm data availability & queries; Grace — sampling config + Console surface; Dylan — short-term mitigation plan (fallback route or approximate attribution) and communications to Acme. I'll coordinate with their SRE and PlatformOps.

I've attached the route-sample.csv and a latency heatmap for context. Also linking our internal playbook: https://docs.redwood.com/internal/observability/instrumentation-gap-playbook

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: route-sample.csv (csv), screenshot-latency-heatmap.png (png)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Instrumentation gaps: per-route cost & latency slices + owner runbook

Thanks Rafa — confirmed I can take the sampling/config and Console surface work. Notes from a quick look:
- The CSV shows many short-circuit routes (prefix matches) that our current sampling excludes by default, which explains low token counts for those route IDs.
- Console currently aggregates at the model+route level in a way that drops zero-token requests; we should show an "estimated cost" row when sampling coverage < 5%.

Immediate plan (Grace):
1) Add a temporary sampling override for the impacted tenant IDs so tail requests are captured for 48 hours. (config change + rollout)
2) Add a Console flag that toggles "Show estimated cost when sampling sparse" — implementation: new front-end badge + small API that returns sampling_coverage pct. Backfill can be a daily job.
3) Deliverables: PR for sampling toggle (backend), UI mock for estimated rows, and a short runbook page with commands to run queries.

I'll try to get the sampling override live by Friday 17:00 PT. Marcus — point me to the canonical query that shows per-route token counts (I want to validate the sampling pct quickly).

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Instrumentation gaps: per-route cost & latency slices + owner runbook

Grace — I'm on the queries. Quick summary of what I ran against prod_telemetry this morning:
- Per-route token counts (last 7d) are in table route_token_rollup. For Acme tenant_id=acme-231 we have 3 routes with <10k tokens but thousands of requests — indicates undercounting at tokenization step.
- Suspected cause: a recent change to router X that short-circuits before tokenization for low-content calls (PR 6789).

Proposed steps (Marcus):
A) Open JIRA-RI-8421 to track a repair for router X; include reproduction steps and sample request IDs from the CSV.
B) For immediate diagnostics, run the following query (one-liner):
   SELECT route_id, COUNT(*) as reqs, SUM(tokens) as tokens FROM prod_telemetry.route_token_rollup WHERE tenant_id='acme-231' AND ts >= now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY route_id ORDER BY reqs DESC;
C) If sampling override is active, we can request a job to reprocess logs for the last 48h to generate estimated token counts (costly, but OK for one tenant).

I've created JIRA-RI-8421 and assigned to infra-team with the notes and sample IDs. Link: https://jira.internal.redwood.com/browse/RI-8421

Marcus Lin
Data Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Instrumentation gaps: per-route cost & latency slices + owner runbook

Thanks all — short note from ops side:
- I'll draft the customer-facing message with the mitigation steps and expected timeline. Plan is to (1) tell Acme we're running a 48h sampling override, (2) offer a one-time reprocess for the last 48h to surface corrected metrics, and (3) set an ETA for the permanent router fix (tracked in RI-8421).
- I'll also prep a rollback message and list of routes impacted in case we see regressions.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
